action: Convene the emergency task force session today as announced. The agenda has five items: (1) Receive Stephanie Morris's real estate presentation on auto row vacancy and property conversion trends — this is the first time the task force has had spatial data on the disruption, and it will inform zoning recommendations. (2) Receive a brief update from Patricia Hawkins on the dealership consolidation timeline — specifically: which transition program are separated workers being directed to, and is the retraining grant pipeline accessible to them on their way out the door? (3) Issue a formal task force recommendation to the full council to extend the delivery license notice period by zero days — the 30-day clock stands, and the task force affirms that delivery operations require a separate license amendment. This is the policy enforcement signal the protests are demanding. (4) Open the floor to community input — I am specifically inviting any community member present who has attended a protest to speak for three minutes, on the record, before the formal record is closed. Nine protests means nine organized constituencies. I am not going to manage them from above. I am going to give them a microphone at a formal proceeding. (5) Announce that the task force will produce a 90-day Economic Resilience Framework with specific metrics: target Gini trajectory, target retraining enrollment, target small business stabilization fund utilization, and a zoning recommendation for auto row properties sitting empty. The framework will be presented at a public session in 90 days. The community has been watching me build process. This tick the process produces a named, dated deliverable. The session is recorded, the minutes are public, and the press contact issues a same-day summary.
